title: Spin-orbit torque-driven synthetic antiferromagnetic oscillator
authors: P. K. Rout, J. Godinho, F. Vilsmeier, R. Salikhov, J. A. Vélez, Z. Šobáň, D. Laroze, O. Gomonay, R. M. Otxoa, C. H. Back, O. Hellwig, J. Wunderlich
abstract: Antiferromagnets offer a promising route toward robust spintronic devices because of their compensated magnetic order and exchange-enhanced spin dynamics. Here, we demonstrate a spin-orbit torque (SOT)-driven antiferromagnetic oscillator based on a nanoconstriction patterned from a synthetic antiferromagnet (SAF). Spin-rectification spectroscopy reveals electrical excitation of both acoustic and optical SAF eigenmodes, whose field and frequency dependences are quantitatively described by an antiferromagnetic resonance model. In addition to these linear eigenmodes, we observe low-field spin-rectification peaks that emerge only above a threshold DC current near the spin-flop transition. Their current-polarity-dependent sign and locking to an injected RF frequency provide electrical spin-rectification signatures consistent with current-selected chiral self-oscillatory dynamics. Micromagnetic simulations reproduce the threshold excitation of SOT-driven self-oscillations and injection locking, while macrospin simulations predict stable and chaotic nonlinear dynamics within the same spin-flop region. We interpret the multi-peak, weakly RF-frequency-dependent responses as a qualitative signature of complex nonlinear dynamics. These results establish SAF nanoconstrictions as an experimentally accessible platform for studying current-driven antiferromagnetic-like oscillator dynamics and motivate future work on nonlinear spintronic devices for signal processing and reservoir-computing concepts.
summary: This work investigates current-driven oscillations in synthetic antiferromagnets using spin-orbit torque. By measuring the spin-rectification voltage ($	ext{V}_{	ext{SRE}}$), the authors demonstrated that self-oscillations emerge above a critical DC current threshold, exhibiting characteristic signatures of injection locking. This establishes SAF nanoconstrictions as a viable platform for studying nonlinear spintronic oscillators.
main_problem: The study aims to demonstrate and characterize spin-orbit torque (SOT)-driven self-oscillatory dynamics in synthetic antiferromagnets (SAFs) using electrical measurements.
main_result: The research successfully identified low-field, current-induced peaks in the spin-rectification voltage ($	ext{V}_{	ext{SRE}}$), interpreted as signatures of current-selected chiral self-oscillations and injection locking near the spin-flop transition.
method: The study combines electrical measurements (spin-rectification spectroscopy) with theoretical modeling, utilizing both micromagnetic simulations and macrospin approximations.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a nanoconstriction patterned from a synthetic antiferromagnet (SAF) multilayer stack. The dynamics are governed by exchange coupling, spin-orbit torque (SOT), and applied DC/RF currents.
key_observables: Spin-rectification voltage ($	ext{V}_{	ext{SRE}}$), acoustic and optical eigenmode resonance frequencies, Power Spectral Density (PSD) features indicating self-oscillation onset and injection locking.
important_parameters: Critical DC current threshold ($J_{above}^{dc}$), applied magnetic field ($\vec{H}$), RF frequency range ($2	ext{ GHz}$ to $12	ext{ GHz}$).
main_assumptions: The observed $	ext{V}_{	ext{SRE}}$ peaks are interpreted as electrical signatures of self-oscillatory dynamics, rather than direct emission detection.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the SAF structure and patterned device; they show distinct resonance peaks for acoustic/optical modes (Fig. 1d); simulation results demonstrate threshold excitation of oscillations in PSDs (Fig. 2b); and $	ext{V}_{	ext{SRE}}$ measurements confirm current-dependent, self-oscillatory signatures (Fig. 3).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the linear eigenmodes via SRE spectroscopy across different angles ($\Phi$). It then investigates nonlinear dynamics by observing that additional peaks appear only when a DC current exceeds a critical threshold, confirming self-oscillation and subsequent injection locking.
why_interesting: While focused on spintronics, the study of driven, non-equilibrium collective excitations (self-oscillations) in magnetic systems shares conceptual links with open quantum system dynamics and nonlinear response theory relevant to AMO physics.
